source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN Examination, 7th ed.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: After vomiting has stopped for 4 hours, what should the nurse offer first?
questions.rationale: Clear liquids are tolerated first, in sips of 20 to 30 mL, such as water or flat ginger ale.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q315 (PDF p. 479)
questions.quote: Clear liquids are best tolerated first after episodes of nausea and vomiting.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: What does the client do as an NG tube is removed?
options: Take a deep breath and hold
questions.rationale: Breath-holding minimizes aspiration of gastric contents spilling from the tube.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q317 (PDF p. 481)
questions.quote: breath-holding minimizes the risk of aspirating gastric contents spilled from the tube during removal.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: What should the nurse check before hanging an intralipid infusion?
questions.rationale: Separation or an oily appearance may mean spoiled or contaminated emulsion.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q318 (PDF p. 482)
questions.quote: The nurse checks the solution for separation or an oily appearance

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: What is the first dressing layer at a chest tube insertion site?
questions.rationale: Petrolatum gauze forms an occlusive seal at the insertion site; gauze layers go on top.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q320 (PDF p. 484)
questions.quote: The first layer of the chest tube dressing is petrolatum gauze

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A clinic client's left-arm BP is 200/118. What should the nurse do NEXT?
options: Take BP in the right arm
questions.rationale: The nurse checks the opposite arm to see if the elevation is limited to one extremity, and rechecks.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q327 (PDF p. 492)
questions.quote: the nurse takes the pressure in the opposite arm

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client due for furosemide and nifedipine requests an antacid. What should the nurse do?
questions.rationale: Antacids interfere with absorption, so they are separated from other drugs by at least 1 hour.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q340 (PDF p. 508)
questions.quote: antacids should be separated from other medications by at least 1 hour.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: What is the safest way to ambulate a client with a nephrostomy tube?
options: Attach it to a leg bag
Carry the bag above the hip
questions.rationale: A leg bag allows movement while protecting tube integrity and drainage.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q362 (PDF p. 530)
questions.quote: The safest approach to protect the integrity and safety of the nephrostomy tube with a mobile client is to attach the tube to a leg collection bag.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: An IV drug is incompatible with the running solution. What should the nurse do?
questions.rationale: The line is flushed with normal saline before and after the drug to prevent in-line precipitation.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q393 (PDF p. 563)
questions.quote: the tubing is flushed before and after the medication with infusions of normal saline

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: How are eardrops given to an infant?
options: Pull the auricle up and back
Pull the auricle down and back
questions.rationale: For children under 3, the auricle is pulled down and back with the affected ear uppermost. Over 3, it is pulled up and back.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q394 (PDF p. 564)
questions.quote: With the nondominant hand, the nurse pulls down and back on the auricle.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: How are eardrops given to a 6-year-old?
options: Pull the ear down and back
Pull the ear up and back
questions.rationale: For children over 3, the ear is pulled upward and back. Gloves are not needed for parents.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q698 (PDF p. 920)
questions.quote: To administer eardrops in a child who is more than 3 years old, the ear is pulled upward and back.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: When is a sputum culture best collected?
questions.rationale: Sputum collects in the airways during sleep, so early morning gives the best specimen, ideally before antibiotics.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q408 (PDF p. 582)
questions.quote: The specimen is obtained early in the morning whenever possible

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Where should the drainage bag be placed after inserting a Foley catheter?
questions.rationale: The bag below bladder level ensures drainage and prevents retrograde flow and infection.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q413 (PDF p. 590)
questions.quote: The drainage bag is placed lower than bladder level to ensure drainage

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: What is done before injecting heparin 5000 units subcutaneously?
questions.rationale: Changing the needle prevents leakage along the needle tract. SC heparin needs no infusion device and the site is not massaged.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q422 (PDF p. 599)
questions.quote: the needle is changed before injection to prevent leakage of medication along the needle tract.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: What should the nurse do FIRST when developing a diabetes teaching program?
questions.rationale: The nurse first assesses clients and their needs to plan effectively.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q445 (PDF p. 625)
questions.quote: the nurse must first assess the clients and their needs to effectively plan the program.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: How does the nurse BEST ensure safe self-medication at home?
options: Have the client explain and demonstrate
questions.rationale: Asking the client to explain and demonstrate shows understanding and skill.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q469 (PDF p. 653)
questions.quote: the nurse asks the client to explain and demonstrate correct self-administration of medication procedures

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: 1000 mL over 8 hours with a drop factor of 15 gtt/mL. What is the rate?
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q477 (PDF p. 663)
questions.quote: Then divide the result by 480 minutes

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which observation shows crutches are fitted correctly?
questions.rationale: The elbow is flexed about 30 degrees on the handgrip, and the crutch top is two to three finger-widths below the axilla.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q511 (PDF p. 706)
questions.quote: the elbow should be at approximately 30 degrees of flexion when the hand is resting on the handgrip.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which shows correct walker use?
options: Slides it while leaning on it
Sets all four legs down, then steps
questions.rationale: The client places all four points of the walker flat about 2 feet forward before putting weight on it and stepping.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q520 (PDF p. 715)
questions.quote: put all four points of the walker 2 feet forward flat on the floor before putting weight on

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Urine flows as the Foley enters the bladder. What does the nurse do NEXT?
questions.rationale: The balloon is behind the tip, so the catheter is advanced 2.5 to 5 cm further before inflating.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q530 (PDF p. 728)
questions.quote: the nurse inserts the catheter 2.5 to 5 cm further after urine begins to flow

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: What is done before suctioning a tracheostomy?
questions.rationale: The client is hyperoxygenated with deep breaths, a bag, or the ventilator's sigh before suctioning, using sterile technique.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q537 (PDF p. 735)
questions.quote: the nurse hyperoxygenates the client

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: How is a sputum specimen for culture collected?
questions.rationale: Culture and sensitivity specimens need sterile technique to identify organisms accurately.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q538 (PDF p. 736)
questions.quote: Sputum specimens for culture and sensitivity testing need to be obtained using sterile techniques

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: An NPH insulin vial has clumps. What should the nurse do?
questions.rationale: NPH is uniformly cloudy; clumping or frosting means loss of potency, so a new vial is used.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q546 (PDF p. 747)
questions.quote: Clumping, frosting, and precipitates a

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: How is a urinalysis specimen obtained from an indwelling catheter?
questions.rationale: The closed system stays sterile; the specimen is aspirated from the port after cleansing.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q551 (PDF p. 752)
questions.quote: the indwelling urinary catheter system must remain sterile to reduce the risk of infection.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which catheter care direction should be given to a nursing attendant?
options: Clean the perineum with soap and water
Lift the bag above the bladder
questions.rationale: The perineal area is cleansed with mild soap and water at least three times a day and after bowel movements.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q552 (PDF p. 753)
questions.quote: The perineal area is cleansed thoroughly using mild soap and water

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A 1000-mL bag hung at 9 am runs at 100 gtt/min by microdrip. How much remains at 2 pm?
questions.rationale: With microdrip, gtt/min = mL/hr, so 100 mL/hr × 5 hr = 500 mL infused; 500 mL remain.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q555 (PDF p. 756)
questions.quote: With a microdrip, gtt/min=mL/hr infused.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A peritoneal dialysis catheter dressing gets wet while bathing. What should be done?
questions.rationale: A wet dressing lets bacteria reach the site; it is changed immediately and kept dry.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q569 (PDF p. 774)
questions.quote: A dressing that is wet is a conduit for bacteria to reach the catheter insertion site.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client with right-sided weakness transfers to a wheelchair. Where is the chair placed?
questions.rationale: Movement is toward the unaffected (left) side so the client can use the strong leg.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q593 (PDF p. 801)
questions.quote: movement should occur toward the client’s unaffected (strong) side

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client with hypoparathyroidism has hyperphosphatemia. Which food should be avoided?
questions.rationale: High-phosphate foods include fish, eggs, milk products, whole grains, and carbonated beverages.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q623 (PDF p. 839)
questions.quote: Food items and liquids that are naturally high in phosphates include fish, eggs, milk products, whole grains

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client gets dizzy using the incentive spirometer. What is the likely cause?
questions.rationale: Not breathing normally between spirometer breaths causes hyperventilation and respiratory alkalosis.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q643 (PDF p. 861)
questions.quote: Hyperventilation is the most common cause of respiratory alkalosis

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which shows a client understands home Foley care?
questions.rationale: The bag stays below the bladder with tubing free of kinks; the perineum is cleaned twice daily.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q646 (PDF p. 864)
questions.quote: The drainage bag of an indwelling urinary catheter should be lower than the level of the bladder

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client weighed 75 kg on admission. Which weight shows adequate nutrition?
questions.rationale: Adequate nutrition means keeping baseline weight or losing less than about 2 kg (5 lb).
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q659 (PDF p. 878)
questions.quote: if the client maintains the baseline body weight or loses less than 5 pounds.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: How should the nurse evaluate a client's learning of IV dressing care?
questions.rationale: Psychomotor skills are best evaluated by observing a return demonstration (teach-back).
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q662 (PDF p. 881)
questions.quote: a teach back method to observe the client performing the skill

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which statement about an implanted port needs MORE teaching?
questions.rationale: An implanted port does not need pumping to stay patent.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q663 (PDF p. 882)
questions.quote: An implanted vascular access port does not need to be pumped to maintain patency.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which meat choice is BEST for a client with hypertension?
questions.rationale: Bacon, hot dogs, luncheon meats, and corned beef are high in sodium.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q669 (PDF p. 888)
questions.quote: Foods from the meat group that are higher in sodium include bacon, hot dogs, luncheon meat

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: How can a home IV client prevent phlebitis and infiltration?
options: Keep the site secured and protected
questions.rationale: Protecting and securing the site keeps the catheter immobile.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q673 (PDF p. 893)
questions.quote: Protecting the IV site and securing it with tape are extremely important

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Where are crutches placed in the tripod standing position?
questions.rationale: In the tripod position, crutches are 6 to 10 inches in front of and to the side of the toes.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q674 (PDF p. 894)
questions.quote: The crutches are placed anywhere from 6 to 10 inches in front of and to the side of the client’s t

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: Where should a mother start when bathing her newborn?
questions.rationale: Bathing starts with the cleanest area, the eyes and face, then ears and neck.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q695 (PDF p. 917)
questions.quote: Bathing should start at the eyes and face and with the cleanest area first.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which incentive spirometer action needs MORE teaching?
questions.rationale: Incentive spirometry is ineffective with nose breathing.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q707 (PDF p. 929)
questions.quote: Incentive spirometry is ineffective if the client breathes through the nose.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which position helps a client with COPD breathe more easily?
questions.rationale: Sitting upright and leaning on an overbed table, or with arms on the chair arms, eases dyspnea.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q708 (PDF p. 930)
questions.quote: Appropriate positions include sitting upright while leaning on an overbed table

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: How much larger than the stoma is the colostomy appliance opening cut?
questions.rationale: 1/8 inch larger minimizes exposed skin without pressing on the stoma.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q792 (PDF p. 1022)
questions.quote: The size of the opening for the appliance is generally cut 1/8 inch larger than the size of the client’s stoma.
